topic: Watkins letter: PSI staff quotation (Skilling's departure)
claim: The Senate subcommittee staff report quotes the letter Sherron Watkins wrote to Kenneth Lay the day after Jeffrey Skilling resigned, warning that his sudden departure would raise suspicions about Enron's accounting.
quote: Sherron Watkins wrote, ‘‘Skilling’s abrupt departure will raise suspicions of accounting improprieties and valuation issues. . . . The spotlight will be on us, the market just can’t accept that Skilling is leaving his dream job.’’
notes: The report dates the letter 8/15/01 (n. 18) and reprints it as Appendix 2 (see F-004). The report's '. . .' omits letter text between the two sentences. Text-layer PDF (not OCR). Wording matches the reprinted letter image (Appendix 2, printed p. 57).
checker_note: Fingerprint OK. Quote verified verbatim in the text layer (rpt-psi-board PDF 16, printed p. 12, lines 853-857). The two quoted sentences also checked against the letter image (App. 2, PDF 61, printed p. 57): wording matches; the report's '. . .' correctly marks omitted text. Claim, verb and source type OK.

topic: Watkins letter: PSI Finding 4 quotations (implode; Raptor and Condor)
claim: The Senate subcommittee staff reported that the directors it interviewed said they saw neither Watkins's letter nor Vinson & Elkins's report on it until after Enron had begun to collapse. The staff wrote that, had they seen it, they would have learned she told Lay in mid-August 2001 that she feared Enron would 'implode' in accounting scandals and that its accounting was 'very aggressive,' especially the Raptor and Condor deals.
quote: Ms. Watkins had told Mr. Lay in mid-August that she was ‘‘incredibly nervous that [Enron] will implode in a wave accounting scandals’’; that ‘‘Enron has been very aggressive in its accounting—most notably the Raptor transactions and the Condor vehicle’’

locator.section: Finding (4), discussion of the Raptors and the Oct. 2001 Board meeting; n. 156

notes: WORDING DISCREPANCY: the staff report's quotation reads 'a wave accounting scandals' (the word 'of' is missing and '[Enron]' replaces 'we'). The letter itself, reprinted as Appendix 2 (printed p. 57, PDF 61, checked against the image), reads 'I am incredibly nervous that we will implode in a wave of accounting scandals.' Writers should quote the letter itself (F-004), not this version. n. 156 explains that the 'Condor vehicle' refers to Whitewing and the Osprey debt certificates. Same passage: interviewed directors said officers referred to the letter at the October 2001 Board meeting as coming from an anonymous employee, and Lay 'apparently did not disclose' its Raptor and accounting concerns to fellow directors (staff finding, based on director interviews).
checker_note: Fingerprint OK. FIXED. Claim said the staff 'found that the outside directors never saw' the letter. The report attributes this to the directors: 'The interviewed directors said that they saw neither the letter itself nor the Vinson & Elkins report on it until after Enron had begun to collapse' (PDF 49, printed p. 45). Reworded the claim to 'the directors ... said' and changed the verb to 'reported'. Quote verified verbatim against the text layer AND the page image (PDF 49): the report really does print 'a wave accounting scandals' (no 'of'). The letter image (App. 2, PDF 61) reads 'I am incredibly nervous that we will implode in a wave of accounting scandals.' The misquote finding is CONFIRMED: quote the letter (F-004), not the report's version. 'Enron has been very aggressive in its accounting—most notably the Raptor transactions and the Condor vehicle' matches the letter.

topic: Watkins letter: PSI Finding 4 quotations (disclosure; footnotes)
claim: The Senate subcommittee staff report quotes Watkins's warning that Enron's related-party footnote did not adequately explain the transactions, and that an investor who understood them would know the entities were thinly capitalized and backed by Enron stock.
quote: My concern is that the footnotes don’t adequately explain the transactions. If adequately explained, the investor would know that the ‘‘Entities’’ described in our related party footnote are thinly capitalized, the equity holders have no skin in the game
notes: Also quoted on this page: 'None of that will protect Enron if these transactions are ever disclosed in the bright light of day.' SMALL DISCREPANCY: the staff report's block quote begins 'The overriding principle of accounting...'; the letter image (App. 2, printed p. 58, PDF 62) reads 'The overriding basic principle of accounting...'. The report also replaces 'AA&Co.' with '[Andersen]'. Directly relevant to the Footnote page: Watkins refers to 'our related party footnote'. The staff then compares the one-page related-party footnotes (Footnote 16) in the 1999 and 2000 10-Ks with the nine-page description in the Q3 2001 10-Q, calling the 2000 footnote 'nearly unintelligible' (same page). SECOND DISCREPANCY (found by the Fact-Checker): the staff report's block quote reads 'Would he buy or sell the stock'; the letter image reads 'Would he sell or buy the stock' (App. 2, printed p. 58, PDF 62).
checker_note: Fingerprint OK. FIXED (notes only). Quote verified verbatim in the text layer (PDF 52, printed p. 48) and against the letter image (App. 2, PDF 62): 'My concern is that the footnotes don't adequately explain the transactions. If adequately explained, the investor would know that the "Entities" described in our related party footnote are thinly capitalized, the equity holders have no skin in the game' matches. The misquote finding is CONFIRMED: the report prints 'The overriding principle of accounting' where the letter reads 'The overriding basic principle of accounting', and replaces 'AA&Co.' with '[Andersen]'. I found one more: 'buy or sell' (report) vs 'sell or buy' (letter); added to notes. Quote the letter image, not the report's block quote, for any of these sentences.

topic: Watkins letter: full text printed in library documents

Page 1 is also printed (tab 10) in the exhibits of the February 14, 2002 hearing. The letter opens by asking whether Enron had become a risky place to work.
quote: Has Enron become a risky place to work? ... I am incredibly nervous that we will implode in a wave of accounting scandals.

locator.section: Appendix 2, 'Sherron Watkins’ Letter to Board Chairman Kenneth Lay (8/15/01)'

notes: The quote joins two sentences from the same page (paragraphs 1 and 6), marked with '...'; use them separately if preferred. PDF pp. 61-63 are images with no text; quotes were read directly from the page images. As printed, the letter is addressed 'Dear Mr. Lay,' and carries no signature; the report's appendix title attributes it to Watkins. Watkins testified she gave Lay 'the anonymous letter on August 15, 2001, and then the full set of memos when we met on August 22, 2001' (hrg-commerce-skilling-watkins, printed p. 87, PDF 91, text lines 5594-5596). OTHER PRINTINGS (image pages, found by OCR in scratch and confirmed against the page images): (a) hrg-hec-collapse-pt4 (Mar. 14, 2002), tab 14, printed pp. 116-118 (PDF 120-122), Bates E 68548-68550: the full three-page letter, same wording as the PSI Appendix 2. topic: Oct. 16, 2001 earnings release: Lay's words
claim: The bankruptcy examiner's First Interim Report quotes Enron's October 16, 2001 earnings release, in which Lay said the 26 percent increase in recurring earnings per share showed 'the very strong results' of Enron's core energy and pipeline businesses and that Enron was 'very confident' in its earnings outlook. In the next paragraph the release disclosed $1.01 billion in after-tax 'non-recurring charges.'
quote: Kenneth Lay, Enron’s Chairman and CEO, stated that “[o]ur 26 percent increase in recurring earnings per diluted share shows the very strong results of our core wholesale and retail energy businesses and our natural gas pipelines” and that Enron is “very confident in our strong earnings outlook.”

locator.section: I.B 'Fall 2001 Events', 'Enron’s October 16, 2001 Earnings Release'; n. 6

source_type: examiner's description (quoting a company press release)
notes: Verified word for word against the page image (PDF p. 4). The examiner is quoting Lay's words in the press release. topic: Enron Code of Conduct: officers' outside interests (PSI)
claim: The Senate subcommittee staff report quotes Enron's code of conduct: no full-time officer or employee could hold an interest in an entity doing business with Enron unless it was disclosed in writing to the Chairman and CEO and he found it did not hurt Enron's best interests. The staff found that Lay approved waiving this rule for Fastow's LJM partnerships and asked the Board to ratify that decision, even though company rules did not explicitly require Board approval.
quote: [N]o full-time officer or employee should . . . [o]wn an interest in or participate, directly or indirectly, in the profits of any other entity which does business with or is a competitor of the Company, unless such ownership or participation has been previously disclosed in writing to the Chairman of the Board
notes: Source of the code text: Hearing Exhibit 26, 'Conflicts of Interest, Investments, and Outside Business Interests of Officers and Employees', at 57 (n. 58). n. 57 quotes the general 'Business Ethics' rule from the same exhibit (7/00) at 12. DISAGREEMENT: n. 59 notes that at the hearing directors Winokur and Jaedicke 'contended that the Board did not actually ‘‘waive’’ the company’s code of conduct, but ‘‘applied’’ it'. The staff answers that all three LJM presentations explicitly asked for a code of conduct waiver. The staff also says evidence from the Andersen criminal trial indicates Board ratification 'may have originated with Andersen' (p. 24). The Board approved waivers for LJM1, LJM2 and LJM3 (p. 23).
checker_note: Fingerprint OK. Quote verified verbatim (rpt-psi-board PDF 28, printed p. 24, n. 58; lines 1613-1618). Claim verified at lines 1580-1583: 'Mr. Lay approved waiving the code of conduct prohibition for Mr. Fastow, but also asked the Enron Board to ratify his decision, even though Board concurrence was not explicitly required by company rules.' The n. 59 disagreement (Winokur/Jaedicke: 'applied', not 'waived') is stated accurately. Staff finding; verb 'found' OK.

topic: Enron Code of Conduct: Board ratification (Powers)
claim: The board's special committee found that Fastow told the Board in June 1999 that LJM1 required action under Enron's Code of Conduct, which was within Lay's authority. The Board adopted a resolution ratifying the Office of the Chairman's determination that Fastow's participation would not adversely affect Enron. The Board later adopted and ratified a similar determination for LJM2.
quote: The resolution ratified a determination by the Office of the Chairman that Fastow's participation in LJM1 would not adversely affect the interests of Enron.

locator.section: III.A LJM1 (Board approval, June 28, 1999); LJM2 approval

notes: Code text in Powers n. 8 (p. 44) matches the PSI quotation (F-006) word for word. The LJM2 resolution language quoted by Powers (p. 72): the Board 'adopt[ing] and ratify[ing]' the Office of the Chairman's determination. Powers p. 4 (line 406): 'We have seen no evidence that any of these employees, except Fastow, obtained the permission required by Enron's Code of Conduct of Business Affairs to own interests in the partnerships.' Powers p. 44 also says in-house counsel and Vinson & Elkins advised Fastow that his participation in Chewco would need Chairman/CEO approval under the Code, so Kopper was substituted as Chewco's manager.

topic: Nancy Temple: role
claim: Nancy Temple was an in-house attorney at Arthur Andersen. She testified under oath before the House Energy and Commerce oversight subcommittee on January 24, 2002. The subcommittee chairman said her mid-October 2001 e-mails reminding Andersen staff of the firm's document retention and destruction policy were 'highly unusual and of questionable timing'.
quote: the now well-publicized e-mails from Ms. Temple to Andersen’s personnel working on Enron matters in the mid-October timeframe to remind them of the firm’s retention and destruction policies were by all accounts highly unusual and of questionable timing.
source_type: congressional hearing statement (subcommittee chairman's opening statement)
notes: The quote is a congressman's opening statement, not testimony and not a finding. Use 'the subcommittee chairman said.' In the same statement he said: 'We have no reason at this point to doubt her good intentions'. Temple was sworn in with the second panel, listed as 'NANCY TEMPLE, ATTORNEY, ANDERSEN LLP' (printed p. 30, PDF 34). She testified that the November 10 memo telling staff not to destroy documents was drafted by outside counsel Davis Polk & Wardwell (text lines 3279-3283). CHARGES: no library document shows that Temple was charged. andersen-scotus (Syllabus only) does not name her. In hrg-hfs-enron-investors (line 9648, Feb. 5, 2002) Rep. Shadegg, questioning Berardino, said memos in the popular press 'suggest' that Temple 'pretty much instructed him to shred'. That is a congressman's remark about press reports, not testimony or a finding. Gap already logged.

topic: Lea Fastow: outcome

quote: In 2003, the Enron Task Force indicted numerous Enron employees, including Ben Glisan, Jr. (the company’s treasurer), Lea Fastow (wife of Andrew and an assistant treasurer) ... In 2004, Andrew and Lea Fastow both pleaded guilty

topic: Richard Buy: role
claim: Richard Buy was Enron's Chief Risk Officer. The board's special committee found that he and Chief Accounting Officer Richard Causey were to review and approve all LJM transactions. It found that neither 'ignored his responsibilities', but both interpreted their roles very narrowly.
quote: while neither the Chief Accounting Officer, Causey, nor the Chief Risk Officer, Buy, ignored his responsibilities, they interpreted their roles very narrowly and did not give the transactions the degree of review the Board believed was occurring.
notes: Powers p. 84 also calls Buy head of Enron's Risk Assessment and Control (RAC) group and Kaminski's supervisor. It records that Buy 'does not recall any discussions with Kaminski' about the Rhythms deal (see F-014). CHARGES: searched all library texts. No indictment, plea, SEC complaint or conviction names Buy as a defendant. The SEC complaints in the library do not mention him. See F-012 for his use of the Fifth Amendment.
checker_note: Fingerprint OK. Quote verified verbatim (Powers p. 10, lines 622-626). topic: Richard Buy: Fifth Amendment before Congress
claim: At a House Energy and Commerce oversight hearing on February 7, 2002, Buy was sworn in with Causey and declined to answer any questions, invoking his Fifth Amendment rights.
quote: Mr. GREENWOOD. And will you invoke your Fifth Amendment rights in response to all of our questions here today, Mr. Buy? Mr. BUY. Yes, I will.

locator.section: Testimony of Richard A. Causey and Richard B. Buy

notes: Invoking the Fifth Amendment is not evidence of guilt; say so if this is used. The chairman described Buy and Causey as 'specifically charged by the board of directors' with making sure LJM transactions were at arm's length. 'Charged' here means 'given the duty', not criminally charged. Avoid that word near Buy's name. No library document shows criminal or SEC charges against Buy.

topic: Vince Kaminski: role
claim: Vincent Kaminski headed Enron's Research Group, which handled complex option pricing and modeling. He told the special committee that he strongly advised his supervisor, Richard Buy, not to go ahead with the 1999 Rhythms/LJM1 transaction. Buy said he did not recall those discussions.
quote: Vincent Kaminski, head of Enron's Research Group--which handled sophisticated option pricing and modeling issues--told us that he was very uncomfortable with the transaction and brought his concerns to Richard Buy

locator.section: IV (Rhythms hedge), C.3 'Pricing and Credit Capacity'

notes: Powers reports sharply different memories here: 'We encountered sharply divergent recollections'. It attributes each account to the person who gave it. Kaminski's three reasons were conflict of interest, a payout skewed against Enron, and an SPE capitalized largely with Enron stock. Powers p. 87 (lines 3251-3256): Kaminski's group later estimated a 68% probability that the Rhythms structure would default. Powers p. 124: he told Andersen and Enron accountants that the Raptor share discount could not be reconciled with the collar. The Fifth Circuit (ca5-skilling-2009, PDF p. 9, n. 5, text lines 327-334) says Kaminski said Skilling told him his group 'acted more like cops' and that after the LJM deal Skilling moved Kaminski's group out of risk control. The Batson Final Report (batson-final, printed p. 19, PDF 22, n. 41; OCR text checked against page image) calls him 'Wincenty Kaminski', a Ph.D. economist, and quotes his sworn statement calling the LJM2/Raptor hedges 'terrible, terrible economic hedges.' CHARGES: none in the library. He appears only as a witness and critic.
checker_note: Fingerprint OK. Quote verified verbatim (Powers pp. 84-85, lines 3147-3162); 'sharply divergent recollections' and each account attributed. The 68% default estimate (lines 3251-3256) and CA5 n. 5 'acted more like cops' (ca5-skilling-2009 PDF 9, lines 327-334) verified. Verb 'stated' is acceptable (the committee reports what Kaminski told it). topic: Oct 16, 2001 release: the $544M charge (what it covered)
claim: The bankruptcy examiner reported that Enron's October 16, 2001 earnings release listed a $544 million after-tax charge that covered losses on certain investments (principally The New Power Company, and broadband and technology investments) together with the early termination of structured finance arrangements with LJM2 (the Raptors).
quote: $544 million “related to losses associated with certain investments, principally Enron’s interest in The New Power Company, broadband and technology investments, and early termination during the third quarter of certain structured finance arrangements with a previously disclosed entity.”

locator.section: I.B Fall 2001 Events - Enron's October 16, 2001 Earnings Release

notes: The examiner is quoting the Oct 16 release. The $544M bucket was not only the Raptors. The 'previously disclosed entity' is LJM2 (p. 3, PDF 5). The same report (p. 4, PDF 6) and the Final Report (n. 29, PDF 18) then attribute the $544M after-tax charge to the Raptor termination, as does Powers (p. 128). Enron's 10-Q gives $462M after tax for the Raptor charges (F-017). Safe wording: 'Enron's October 16 announcement included a $544 million after-tax charge that covered the Raptors and some investment losses.'
checker_note: Fingerprint OK. OCR quote checked against page images PDF 4-5: verbatim (the quote runs across the page break; the footnote marker 7 after 'Company,' is omitted).  Round 3 Fact-Checker A.

topic: Raptor charge after tax per the Q3 2001 10-Q
claim: In its Q3 2001 quarterly report, Enron reported charges of $710 million ($462 million after tax) related to acquiring the Raptor SPEs, plus a separate $48 million ($31 million after tax) write-down of NPW warrants, after paying about $35 million for LJM's interests.
